At Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event held today, the company confirmed the rollout timeline for the new Siri AI, which will debut in English first before expanding to five additional languages in October. Here's what you need to know.

Siri AI language expansion confirmed for October launch

Beyond unveiling the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple today also announced its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo. The company additionally launched the Apple Watch Series 12 Ultra 4, as well as the AirPods 5 with active noise cancellation.

The common thread across all these devices is that they rely on one or more features of the new Siri AI — a more powerful large language model assistant delivered through Apple's partnership with Google.

Following Siri AI's debut at WWDC earlier this year, Apple today provided further details on the specific rollout plans for the languages it will support.

Lilian Rincon, Apple's Vice President of Product Marketing for AI, said at the event that the new Siri AI will launch in English on the same day iOS 27 rolls out (tentatively September 14), with support for the following languages opening up陆续 in October:

  • French
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish

Rincon also confirmed two pieces of information first mentioned by Apple's Craig Federighi at WWDC earlier this year.

First, certain features will have usage caps, as they rely on powerful server-side models, and most iCloud+ plans will be allocated higher usage allowances.

Second, Apple Intelligence (of which Siri AI is just one part) will support the following 16 languages in this month's operating system updates:

  • English
  • Simplified Chinese
  • Traditional Chinese
  • Danish
  • Dutch
  • French
  • German
  • Italian
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Norwegian
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish
  • Swedish
  • Turkish
  • Vietnamese

Apple noted that Apple Intelligence is not available in China, but it appears the company is working behind the scenes to bring these features to the Chinese market. Apple also stated that Siri AI will not be available in China and the EU — the latter due to ongoing disagreements between Apple and regulators over the Digital Markets Act.
